source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference Reveals Working Memory Limits in LLMs Beyond Context Length
finding: PI-LLM task: a stream of key-value updates, ask only for the latest value per key. Accuracy falls log-linearly as the number of old values per key grows, for every model tested. Errors are old values of the same key, not search failures.
numbers: 46 keys, 400 values per category, 0.6B to 637B params, dense and MoE, GPT/Claude/Gemini/Grok/Llama/Qwen. Update count swept from a few to about 400; accuracy goes toward 0 at the top. Bootstrap CI95.
quote: Search is straightforward, so errors can be attributed primarily to interference rather than search difficulty
limits: Synthetic word pairs. Single task type.
agent_relevance: Every similar entry stored under one cue is a distractor for the newest one. Cap similar entries per cue; do not rely on the model to pick the latest.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference Reveals Working Memory Limits in LLMs Beyond Context Length (error stages)
finding: Errors move through three stages as interference grows: errors near the true value (adjacent old updates), then errors spread to far earlier updates, then values never shown (hallucination) plus a primacy bias to the first updates.
numbers: 11 equal position bins; the share of off-values and off-keys rises with update count (Fig 5, Fig 19).
limits: Binned description, not a per-model table. Hallucination share is given only qualitatively in the text.
agent_relevance: Wrong answers under heavy overload shift from stale-but-real to invented. A checker should test that an answer exists in the source memory.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference Reveals Working Memory Limits in LLMs Beyond Context Length (size vs context)
finding: Interference resistance (IES, area under the accuracy curve over log update count) tracks parameter count, not context window length.
numbers: Regression on 30 open models: size class t=3.03, p=0.005; context length t=-0.144, p=0.886; R2=0.261. Models with 128k-131k context (N=19): Spearman 0.673, p=0.0016.
limits: Closed-model parameter counts excluded. Later work (c07) found a weaker size link for PI (R2=0.06) with 39 models incl. many MoE.
agent_relevance: Buying a longer context window does not buy resistance to near-duplicate entries. Plan on the same cap at any window length.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference Reveals Working Memory Limits in LLMs Beyond Context Length (other load axes)
finding: Raising the number of tracked keys, the number of updated keys, or the length of each value produces the same log-linear drop; value length hurts most. Interpreted as one shared anti-interference resource.
numbers: Value length 1 to 10 words: accuracy below 40% for every model. 40 words: below 5%. Updated-keys vs tracked-keys manipulations at fixed update counts 125 and 350 gave only minor differences.
limits: The one-resource reading is the authors' interpretation; no mechanistic probing.
agent_relevance: Long entries make interference worse. Store short atomic facts per class, not long notes.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference Reveals Working Memory Limits in LLMs Beyond Context Length (mitigation prompts)
finding: Telling the model to forget old values or to focus on recent ones barely helps. A per-key forget instruction moved errors to the position of the instruction. A fake finished Q&A turn inserted 120 updates before the end (mock QA reset) partly helps.
numbers: Per-key forget, forward focus, soft session reset, relevance meta-prompt: under 10 percentage points gain over baseline at 100 updates. Mock QA reset: partial gain (size only in a figure, not stated in text).
quote: natural language instructions--whether to forget or focus--do not effectively reduce interference
limits: Mock reset is ad hoc and only partial. No numeric table for its gain in the text.
agent_relevance: Do not count on 'ignore the old entries' text. Remove or segment old entries in code. A closed-turn boundary is a cheap partial fix to test.

source: Wang & Sun (2025) Unable to Forget: Proactive Interference Reveals Working Memory Limits in LLMs Beyond Context Length (human comparison)
finding: Authors say humans plateau after some interference (citing Oberauer & Vockenberg 2009) because they unbind outdated associations, while LLM curves keep falling. Humans also use directed-forgetting instructions (Festini & Reuter-Lorenz 2014).
numbers: No new human sample is reported in the text I read; human claims rest on cited work.
limits: Human side is a citation-based contrast, not a matched experiment.
agent_relevance: Humans release old items by control processes; an agent must do this with code (supersede flags, eviction).

source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) LLMs Remember First, Forget Last: Dual-Process Interference in Large Language Models
finding: AB-AC style test on 39 LLMs with identical stimuli: asking for the first value (RI) versus the latest value (PI). All 39 models are worse at PI than RI. This is the reverse of the usual human result.
numbers: N in {3,10,50,100,200,300} assignments per category, 46 categories. RI mean accuracy 93.9% at N=3, 96.0% at N=50, 72.9% at N=100, 45.5% at N=200, 24.6% at N=300. PI falls from about 94% to 3%. Mean RIES-PIES gap 69.5 points, paired t(38)=10.71, d=1.73.
limits: Single paradigm, temperature 0, synthetic category-value pairs. Mechanism claims (attention sink, superposition) are post hoc.
agent_relevance: Old entries beat new ones. When a fact changes, the stale value wins in many models. Always mark superseded entries and drop them.

source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) LLMs Remember First, Forget Last: Dual-Process Interference in Large Language Models (scaling, reasoning)
finding: Model size predicts RI resistance but hardly PI resistance. Reasoning models are best at RI and bad at PI.
numbers: RIES vs params R2=0.491 (p<0.0001); context length R2=0.003; PIES vs params R2=0.06 (p=0.14). RI vs PI correlation r=0.21 (CI -0.11 to 0.49). Reasoning models RIES 178.0 vs 150.3 (d=1.76). o1: RIES 186.4, PIES 22.0 (rank 1 vs 35). Claude-4.5-opus RIES 178.4, PIES 170.3.
limits: n=39; closed-model parameter counts are estimates; MoE total params overstate capacity.
agent_relevance: Thinking longer does not fix the latest-value problem. Pick a model for state tracking by testing PI, not by reasoning rank.

source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) LLMs Remember First, Forget Last: Dual-Process Interference in Large Language Models (errors)
finding: Error types differ. RI errors are mostly empty answers; PI errors are mostly confident intrusions of earlier values from the same key. Real fabrication is rare. Models rarely signal doubt.
numbers: 5,409 RI errors and 9,753 PI errors across 54 models. RI: 50.8% retrieval failure, 46.0% same-key intrusion. PI: 42.5% retrieval failure, 56.1% same-key intrusion. Hallucination 0.9% (RI) and 0.2% (PI). Refusals 8.6% of PI failures, 0% of RI. Over 97% of wrong retrievals carry no uncertainty signal.
limits: Algorithmic classifier plus an LLM judge for refusals.
agent_relevance: The wrong answer is a real stored value, so a format check will not catch it. Need a version or timestamp check in code.

source: Chattaraj & Raj (2026) LLMs Remember First, Forget Last: Dual-Process Interference in Large Language Models (bimodal and decay shapes)
finding: PI decay is near-universal log-linear. RI decay shapes vary by model. At N>=200 PI results flip between near-ceiling and near-floor across sessions.
numbers: Best-fit RI curve: exponential 35% of models, polynomial 30%, log-quadratic 26%, power-law 9%. PI at N>=200 bimodal across sessions.
limits: Adaptive stopping with bootstrap CI below 0.10; reasoning models capped at 20 sessions.
agent_relevance: Under heavy overload a single run is unreliable. One sample of a PI-heavy lookup can be right or wrong; do not trust one draw.

source: Janik (2023) Aspects of human memory and Large Language Models
finding: GPT-J forgets by interference much more than by simple decay. A slow decline appears with list length (decay analogue), but distractor facts about the same people reduce recall far more, and remove the recency effect.
numbers: Decay (extra neutral text) gives a slow decline with n; interference (conflicting or complementary facts about the same persons) gives a much larger drop; baseline distractor was 10 repetitions of 'Humpty Dumpty'. Exact percentages are in figures (Fig 6, 7), not in text.
quote: interference decreases recall accuracy much stronger than decay
limits: One open model (GPT-J) and one list-of-facts design; numbers only in plots.
agent_relevance: Same-entity distractors matter more than added unrelated text. Cap by entity or class, not only by total size.

source: Cao, Schooler & Zafarani (2025) Analyzing Memory Effects in LLMs through the Lens of Cognitive Psychology
finding: Fan-effect test (person-location facts): recognition accuracy falls as the number of facts per item rises, like humans. LLMs show no serial-position curve, unlike humans.
numbers: Fan value 1 to 2 at list size 32: accuracy 0.991 to 0.915. Seven effects tested (list length, list strength, fan, nonsense, position, DRM false memory, cross-domain). Position test: perfect recall regardless of order.
limits: Short lists, simple facts, several models incl. offline Mistral and Llama; some fluctuations; effects are small at these lengths.
agent_relevance: Cue overload in LLMs is real but small at short lengths; it grows with length (c01). Keep per-cue counts low.

source: Roberts et al. (2024) LLM Recall Uncertainty is Modulated by the Fan Effect
finding: Token-probability uncertainty on present/absent follows a human-like fan effect in Mistral and SOLAR, but only for absent items. Items present in context show no fan effect (uncertainty gone). RoBERTa, GPT-2, Llama-2 showed none; Llama-3 slight.
numbers: In-context test with population of N=50 model copies, median aggregation; significant negative Pearson correlations (r>0.3) for absent items in Mistral and SOLAR; a noise floor at probability 0.35.
limits: Measures probability, not accuracy or response time. Two models only. Authors could not make present-item retrieval uncertain.
agent_relevance: Fan effect appears in confidence, so low-probability answers may signal crowded cues. Use only as a weak hint.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: Experience-Following Behavior
finding: Agents copy retrieved experiences: high input similarity gives high output similarity. Adding every experience hurts. Selective add (strict) and selective delete help. Errors in stored records propagate.
numbers: RegAgent success: fixed memory 67.53, add-all 55.48 (4,100 records), strict-selective 70.95 (2,938). AgentDriver: fixed 40.11, add-all 32.32, strict 51.00. EHRAgent accuracy: add-all 13.05, strict 38.50. CIC-IoT: add-all 59.90, strict 85.40. GPT-4o-mini agents.
limits: Strict evaluator is a human oracle; automatic coarse evaluators gave mixed results.
agent_relevance: Best machine-side match for 'cap similar entries': unfiltered growth lowers success by about 8 to 25 points versus selective storage. Add only checked entries.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents (deletion)
finding: Periodic deletion cuts memory a lot with small loss. History-based deletion (drop records whose retrievals led to poor results) helps with a reliable evaluator and can beat an error-free memory baseline in AgentDriver.
numbers: Table 2 compares periodic, history-based and combined deletion; with noisy evaluators history deletion becomes unstable. Exact table values not copied here.
limits: Needs a reliable utility signal; depends on evaluator.
agent_relevance: Retention rule: delete entries by outcome, not age alone.

source: Ding et al. (2026) Controlled Memory Interference in Continual LLM Agents (CMI)
finding: Adding unrelated memories barely changes whether an agent adopts a valid update. Adding repeated history or same-slot conflicts sharply lowers it, with little gain in stability. The relationship, not the count, sets the damage.
numbers: Baseline plasticity 0.84, stability 0.92 (count 0). Count 8, lexical retrieval: unrelated -0.02, repeated history -0.34, same-slot conflict -0.50. Dense retrieval: unrelated -0.18, repeated -0.46, same-slot -0.44. Dense same-slot conflict stability 0.92 to 0.54. Four other encoders: Recall@3 loss 0.22-0.68 (repeated), 0.42-0.58 (same-slot). 50 TravelPlanner base scenarios, DeepSeek-v4-pro.
limits: One main domain (TravelPlanner) plus four others; one generator; controlled transformations, not native benchmark scores.
agent_relevance: Direct support: near-duplicates of the same slot are the harmful kind. Group by slot and keep the latest, or version them.

source: Ding et al. (2026) CMI (poisoning, repair)
finding: Misleading old memories are accepted more when they look like persistent updates or carry authority wording than when merely recent. A lexical/dense router and CMI-made training data improve target access in noisy-update cases.
numbers: Fixed-L3 poison tests, 100 cases per access and condition; P0 control, P1 recency, P2 update wording, P3 authoritative correction. Travel noisy-update answer gain +0.300; unnoised change under 0.005 with CI including zero.
limits: Router is exploratory, trained on oracle labels. Preference ordering did not improve everywhere.
agent_relevance: Hybrid retrieval chosen by simple signals (duplicate density, score margin) is cheap. Authority words in old notes raise their pull; strip them.

source: Lee et al. (2026) MINTEval: Memory under Multi-Target Interference in Long-Horizon Agent Systems
finding: Memory agents and RAG fail on dense, updated contexts. Latest-value questions are easiest; lookback and aggregation questions are much worse. Timestamps repair much of the lookback loss.
numbers: Six systems average 27.7% accuracy, best 33.4%. Simple 47.5%, History 21.0%, multi-target 26.5%. Evidence is in the retrieved pool in only 58.3% of cases; answer errors add a 25.2% drop. SimpleMem with Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite: 30.3 EM. Insert is 87.6% (AtomMem) and 65.9% (Mem-) of memory operations; Mem- modifies 34.1% vs AtomMem 3.7%.
limits: Analytical benchmark; systems differ in backbone; no single method wins across domains (MemAgent 85.7% on bAbI Simple but 7.5% on HorizonBench).
agent_relevance: Memory tools append and rarely delete, so duplicates pile up. Add date or version tags to every fact; tell the agent to edit, not append.

source: Lee et al. (2026) MINTEval (distractors, chunk size, timestamps)
finding: More distractors lower accuracy, most for RAG. In-domain (same-style) distractors hurt aggregation and history questions most. Fewer memory update steps (bigger chunks) help MemAgent. Adding date/time cues removes most of the lookback drop.
numbers: Distractors inserted: 1, 3, 5 sentences, in-domain vs out-of-domain, on bAbI. Date/time cues on facts and questions largely remove the drop as lookback distance grows (Fig 8, size only in figure).
limits: bAbI-based; exact deltas shown in figures only.
agent_relevance: Cheap fix to test: add timestamps (a category-like cue) to every stored entry.

source: Nakshatri et al. (2025) When Facts Change: Probing LLMs on Evolving Knowledge with evolveQA
finding: Old true facts act as distractors for new ones. Models give the outdated answer often in open questions, yet pick the right one in multiple choice, so the new fact is stored but poorly prioritised.
numbers: 12 LLMs, 4 families; AWS 550, Azure 203, WHO 169 QA pairs. Accuracy drops 6% to 31% vs non-conflicting control. MCQ 53-76% vs open-ended 12-51%. Outdated response rate 23-54%. In 32-45% of cases the open answer is outdated but the MCQ is right. With outdated facts as MCQ distractors: about 15% drop (GPT-4.1-mini).
limits: Parametric (trained-in) conflicts, not in-context lists; judge was Claude Sonnet 4 (95.9% agreement with humans on 100 items).
agent_relevance: Showing the model a short list of current vs old choices helps. A 'which of these is current' step may beat free recall.

source: Feng et al. (2026) Tracking the Limits of Knowledge Propagation (TRACK)
finding: Giving updated facts in context can make multi-step reasoning worse than giving none, and it gets worse as more updated facts are added.
numbers: Qwen-3 1.7B Append on WIKI: score 83.6% at KAS=1 down to 22.2% at KAS=500. Qwen-3 8B Append-T: 73.6% down to 11.2%. GPT-4.1-mini stayed stable.
limits: Metric is a reasoning-faithfulness score (HP); some models resilient.
agent_relevance: Context stuffing with many updates is itself interference. Pass only the slot-relevant update.

source: Kerestecioglu et al. (2026) Human-Inspired Memory Architecture for LLM Agents
finding: A deployed-style agent memory adds interference-based forgetting (retroactive weight 0.6, proactive 0.4) with decay. On LongMemEval its variants did not beat raw RAG at small scale.
numbers: S-tier overall accuracy: raw RAG 78.4 [74.8,82.0]; dedup-only 76.8; aggressive consolidation 48.4 [44.0,52.8]; adaptive-10K 57.0. Preference questions 56.7 to 70.0 with dedup (CI wide, not significant).
limits: Weights 0.6/0.4 are design choices from the human literature, not fitted. Forgetting did not help at 50 sessions.
agent_relevance: Aggressive merge destroys detail; dedup is safe but gives no gain at small scale. Do not add forgetting before a measured need.

source: Li & Li (2026) What Should an Agent Forget? Separating What Is Stored from What Is Used (RD-Forget)
finding: Keep old facts in an archive, but hide superseded values from current-state questions through same-slot replacement links; make them eligible again for history questions.
numbers: Fact consolidation gains over best baseline: 11.00 to 26.00 percentage points across four backbones; five task suites. Ablation without forgetting scored lowest.
limits: Abstract and introduction read only; training-free, needs an LLM curator.
agent_relevance: The supersede-not-delete pattern: a slot key with a current pointer and a history archive.

source: SleepGate (2026) Learning to Forget: Sleep-Inspired Memory Consolidation for Resolving Proactive Interference in LLMs
finding: A learned gate tags superseded KV-cache entries and softly suppresses them. In a tiny trained transformer it keeps near-perfect retrieval to 10 prior updates, then collapses; all five cache-compression baselines stay near zero.
numbers: 793K-parameter, 4-layer transformer, synthetic. SleepGate accuracy/stale%: n=1 82.5/0.0, n=5 99.5/0.0, n=10 97.0/3.5, n=15 73.5/23.5, n=20 30.5/55.5, n=30 16.5/62.0. Baselines at n=1: StreamingLLM 17.5, sliding window 12.5, decay only 9.5, full cache 8.0, H2O 6.5. N=200 episodes per depth.
limits: Proof of concept only; not tested on pretrained models; authors note the depth-15 cliff.
agent_relevance: Supports the design: detect same-slot conflicts and suppress stale entries. Plain decay alone fails.

source: Chroma (2025) Context Rot (secondary write-ups)
finding: Reported: 18 frontier models degrade as input grows; one topically close distractor lowers accuracy below needle-only, four compound it; needles with low question similarity degrade faster.
numbers: Secondary summaries only; no exact figures confirmed.
limits: Original report not opened; similarity result described as limited data.
agent_relevance: Same direction as c01; verify before citing numbers.

source: Li, Ding & Hu (2026) Understanding Generalization and Forgetting in In-Context Continual Learning
finding: Theory for linear attention: sequential tasks in one prompt create inter-task interference, a bias-variance-interference split of error, and order sensitivity.
numbers: Abstract read; no empirical numbers used.
limits: Linear and masked linear attention only; theory.
agent_relevance: Gives a reason why long mixed prompts degrade and why order matters.

source: Zhu et al. (2026) Hybrid Self-evolving Structured Memory for GUI Agents (HyMem)
finding: Mixing similar and diverse retrieved trajectories beats pure similarity retrieval in a GUI agent.
numbers: 10 trajectories: 5 seeds by similarity plus 5 graph neighbours gave the best success in all three domains: Amazon 63.4%, Coursera 54.8%, GMap 53.7% (the other two settings were lower). Memory graph size 500 to 1,000 trajectories lifted Amazon 19.5% to 31.7%.
limits: Only three web domains; vision-language agent; per-cue count not controlled.
agent_relevance: Practical analogue of varying the category: retrieve across clusters, not top-k all alike.

source: Decocted Experience Improves Test-Time Inference in LLM Agents (2026)
finding: Retrieved context works best when it balances relevance and diversity; moderate consolidation of memory beats full memory; raw experience degrades as K grows while distilled lessons stay robust.
numbers: Quality score = relevance + lambda x diversity; correlation with performance gain r=0.25, peaking near lambda=0.6. Consolidation shows a sweet spot at intermediate memory size; a very small memory loses information.
limits: Correlation is modest; math and web tasks; k-means consolidation.
agent_relevance: Supports a diversity term in retrieval (e.g. MMR) and consolidation of near-duplicates, not deep compression.

source: Chao et al. (2026) STALE: Can LLM Agents Know When Their Memories Are No Longer Valid?
finding: Even strong models fail to treat a stale memory as stale when the update is implicit. They accept false premises built on old states.
numbers: 400 conflict scenarios, 1,200 queries, contexts up to 150K tokens. Best model (Gemini-3.1-pro) 55.2% overall; Qwen3.5-27B 31.3%. Judge agreement with humans 95.8%.
limits: Abstract and main table read; implicit conflicts only.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on the model to notice that an old entry no longer holds. Code-side supersede logic is needed.
